_source: n8n OpenAPI spec v1.1.1 — GET /api/v1/data-tables + GET /api/v1/data-tables/{id}/rows
_note: Data Tables are structured data storage within n8n. They reveal what data the company tracks alongside their automations.

_query_params.search: free text search across string columns

_llm_can_infer: Table names reveal what data the company actively tracks ('Customer Escalations', 'Failed Payments Log')
Column schemas show the data model — what fields matter to the business
Column types indicate data sophistication (dates, booleans, numbers = structured tracking)
Project ownership shows which team manages which data
Table creation dates show when data tracking started — business timeline
Row data (if queried) shows actual operational volume and patterns

_business_value.data_landscape: Data tables reveal what the company tracks OUTSIDE of workflow data. 'Failed Payments Log' = they monitor payment failures. 'Customer Escalations' = they track support escalations. This enriches the business narrative.
_business_value.process_evidence: A 'Failed Payments Log' table is EVIDENCE that billing is a concern. The LLM can reference this: 'You already track failed payments in a data table — our recommendation to automate recovery builds on data you already collect.'
_business_value.volume_estimation: Row counts per table (from pagination) give volume hints without querying individual rows. 500 rows in 'Failed Payments' = significant payment failure volume.
_business_value.cross_reference: Tables referenced in workflow nodes (via the Data Table node type) create links between automation logic and stored data.
